title: Uniform cohomological bound for oriented nearby cycles
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $f:X\to S$ be a finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] all of whose geometric fibres have dimension at most $d\ge0$, and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring with $m\Lambda=0$ for an integer $m\geq1$ invertible on $S$. For every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $R^i\Psi_fF=0$ for $i>2d$, with $R\Psi$ as in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. If $K$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$, then $R\Psi_fK$ has cohomology only in $[a,b+2d]$. These bounds hold also after every scheme base change $T\to S$, with $T$ arbitrary (not necessarily Noetherian): for $f_T:X_T\to T$, every sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{T,\mathrm{Et}}$ and every complex on $X_{T,\mathrm{Et}}$ with cohomology in $[a,b]$, with the same $d,a,b$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, pp. 3--4; bounded-complex consequence by truncation. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary scheme map $g:T\to S$ and put $f_T:X_T=X\times_ST\to T$. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2), $f_T$ is of finite type, hence locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $t\in T$ and $s=g(t)$. If the fibre $(X_T)_t$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is empty its dimension is $-\infty$. Otherwise pick $x'\in(X_T)_t$; by the first clause of [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] (applied to $f$, which is locally of finite type, and $g$), $(X_T)_t\cong X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. The fibre $X_s$ is of finite type over $\kappa(s)$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2) applied to $f$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$. By [def-weil-geometric-fibre] the geometric fibre is $X_{\bar s}=X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\overline{\kappa(s)}$. Two applications of [lem-kun-dimension-extension] (with $L=\overline{\kappa(s)}$ and with $L=\kappa(t)$, the residue map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)$ being a field extension) give $\dim(X_T)_t=\dim X_s=\dim X_{\bar s}\le d$; here the dimension of [def-kun-dimension] is the topological Krull dimension of the underlying space [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and an isomorphism of schemes is a homeomorphism. So every scheme-theoretic fibre of $f_T$ has topological Krull dimension at most $d$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, p. 3: hypothesis 'fibres de dimension inférieure à N' for an arbitrary base S, verified for f_T

proof.text: Since $m\Lambda=0$, the unit map $\mathbf Z\to\Lambda$ factors through $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$, so $\Lambda$ is a commutative $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$-algebra. By Step 1, [lem-trf-gabber-nearby-cycle-dimension-bound] applies to $f_T$ with $N=d$ (it assumes no Noetherian hypothesis, no invertibility of $m$ and no quasi-compactness). For every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{T,\mathrm{Et}}$ it gives $\mathcal H^i(R\Psi_{f_T}(F[0]))=0$ for $i>2d$. For $T=S$, $g=\mathrm{id}$, this is the first assertion, writing $R^i\Psi_fF=\mathcal H^i(R\Psi_f(F[0]))$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, p. 3: H^i Psi_f F = 0 for i > 2N, after arbitrary base change

proof.text: By [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], $R\Psi_{f_T}=R\psi_{f_T,*}$ is the K-injective total right derived functor of the module direct image $\psi_{f_T,*}:\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{X_{T,\mathrm{Et}}})\to\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{V_{f_T}})$. This functor is additive and left exact, being a right adjoint by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], and both module categories are Grothendieck abelian with K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Hence [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] makes $R\Psi_{f_T}$ an exact triangulated functor commuting with shifts. For a sheaf $F$, $F[0]$ is bounded below with no cohomology in negative degrees, so [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] gives $\mathcal H^i(R\Psi_{f_T}(F[0]))=0$ for $i<0$. With Step 2, $\mathcal H^i(R\Psi_{f_T}(F[0]))=0$ for $i\notin[0,2d]$, for every $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$.

source.place: Section 2.2, p. 3: Psi_f K a priori in D^+, lands in D^b by Proposition 2.3

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-bounded-heart-amplitude] to $T'=R\Psi_{f_T}:D(X_{T,\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)\to D(V_{f_T},\Lambda)$, exact triangulated by Step 3, with $\mathcal S$ the class of all $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $X_{T,\mathrm{Et}}$ (closed under isomorphism, contains $0$) and $[c,d']=[0,2d]$, the hypothesis being Step 3. For $K\in D(X_{T,\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ with $\mathcal H^r(K)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$, $a\le b$, it gives $\mathcal H^i(R\Psi_{f_T}K)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b+2d]$. If $a>b$, $K$ is acyclic, so $K\cong0$ in the derived category and $R\Psi_{f_T}K\cong0$. Taking $T=S$ gives the second assertion; since $T\to S$ was arbitrary, with the same $d,a,b$, both bounds hold after every base change, including non-Noetherian $T$.

source.place: Section 2.2 and Proposition 2.3, p. 3: bounded-complex consequence by truncation
